trent-devex: Heads-up: while wireframing a new Next.js starter for an eval-harness + chat demo I hit two DX surprises: (1) JS SDK treats 401 as terminal in browser bundles, breaking ephemeral token flows; (2) the sample's demo page streams an embedding call and a chat call concurrently and the UI sometimes shows no incremental tokens. Repro and notes below.

mia-frontend: Ack. Short repro please.

trent-devex: Minimal reproduction in sample: 
```js
// pages/index.js (client)
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, retry: { retries: 1 } });
// start embeddings and stream chat concurrently
const emb = client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood/embed-small', input });
const chatStream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood/mini-stream', input: prompt });
for await (const chunk of chatStream) { append(chunk.text); }
await emb;
```
Locally with ephemeral dev tokens the embeddings request gets 401 then 200; the browser SDK surfaces the 401 and stops. Python SDK retries and hides the transient failure. Also, when both calls run concurrently the chat stream sometimes never yields incremental chunks; network shows chunks arriving but the SDK helper yields them bundled or only final text.

otto-ml: Sounds like two separate problems: auth retry policy + stream framing granularity. Any stack traces?

trent-devex: No stack, just early error. I instrumented the fetch wrapper: browser build classifies 401 as non-retriable; our Node bundle includes an auth-refresh hook that retries, the browser doesn't. For streaming, the helper aggregates decoder output until a newline then emits; on Edge/modern browsers the decoder returns grouped bytes so the helper only emits at newline or EOF. Python uses SSE parsing and emits token-sized events.

mia-frontend: For onboarding samples we want things "just work". Proposed short term: update sample to (A) set retry: { retries: 1, authRetry: true } with a one-line comment; (B) avoid concurrent live streams by awaiting embeddings first or cloning responses; (C) use a small incremental decoder shim when using the SDK stream helper on Edge.

clara-docs: Docs change: add an "Edge & ephemeral tokens" section in sample README explaining auth races, and a short snippet with `retry.authRetry: true`. Also document `stream.raw: true` option as an escape hatch.

otto-ml: For SDK: add opt-in flags only. Suggest `retry: { authRetry: boolean }` and `stream: { granularity: 'lines'|'tokens'|'raw' }`. Default keep current behavior. Add an integration test that simulates 401->200 and chunk aggregation.

trent-devex: I'll open two tiny PRs: 1) sample patch that applies the sample-side workarounds + README (INF-8008); 2) SDK patch that adds opt-in flags + tests (INF-8009). Sample will use the shim until SDK ships.

mia-frontend: For the sample shim, can you include a small TextDecoder pump example and mention that Node/dev server behaves differently than Vercel Edge? People will use Vercel preview and be surprised.

clara-docs: Also add a small troubleshooting FAQ: "If you see no streaming tokens in Vercel preview, run locally with `NODE_ENV=development` or use the shim." That seems to cut down onboarding issues.

otto-ml: CI: add an eval harness test that mocks the transport to send token-sized chunks then aggregated chunks and assert the consumer sees the same sequence of text events. This will prevent regressions when we tweak granularity.

ci-bot: [ci] created job 8011: examples/next-eval-starter smoke test (queued)

trent-devex: Thanks all. I'll include a small note in the changelog and ping reviewers. Planning to keep opt-ins off by default and flip after telemetry. Will also include a minimal example for Python parity in the sample repo.

mia-frontend: Great. Ping me for a sample review and I'll help polish the docs copy. :+1:
